idea: Quarterly contrarian screen with analyst notes
buyer: Value-oriented PMs and self-directed sophisticated investors
pain: Screens produce noise; nobody does the work on the outputs
v1: One quarterly screen with five written follow-ups
verdict: Weak on every axis that matters: no clear buyer with budget and a price that cannot reach the target.

why.distribution: Falls between two buyers: institutions want more, retail wants cheaper, and neither is a warm channel at this price.
why.demand: Inferred, and screens with commentary are abundant and largely free.
why.fmf: Squarely her domain, though contrarian value work is a style rather than a credential she holds.
why.revenue_structure: Monthly subscription with the usual newsletter churn.
why.defensibility: Screens are commodity; the writing is the only differentiator.
why.leverage: Media economics, one output for all.
why.time_to_revenue: Needs an audience before anyone pays: 6-9 months.
why.tailwind: Flat, and value screening is well served already.
why.ceiling: £250/mo x 66 subscribers = £198k, which needs an audience she does not have.

ceiling_arithmetic: £250/mo x 66 subscribers = £198k. From zero audience, 66 paying subscribers at this price in year one is not a base case; 15-25 = £45-75k.
kills: No defined buyer with a budget, and a price stranded between institutional and retail.
test: Publish two screens free and see whether anyone asks for more.
test_pass: Unprompted requests for a paid version.
